implement.note: Code to a spec with one check. gpt-implementer (newest Sol, medium) writes all code by default; the Opus verifier reviews it. When Codex is truly empty (real 429s or usage-limit errors, never a low percentage), sonnet-implementer (newest Sonnet, high) stands in first and codex_empty_fallback gives the order; opus-seat takes judgment code by name and whatever Sonnet fails. The factory fold re-seats a piece after two infra failures: Sol or Luna to sonnet-implementer, then opus-seat. route's auditor rule 1 still applies: with the Codex pool empty, Sol is out and no Claude-authored entry has its Sol auditor (a Codex pool at one eligible account already skips the Claude entries), so route picks nothing and the fold's stand-in order decides. orch-lab E12 (2026-09-28, E10 units, n=6 per batch, provisional): Sol medium 6/6 at 379k fresh tokens and $0.86 per accepted unit; Sonnet 5.5 high 8/12 at 565k and $2.76; Opus medium 4/6 at 683k and $3.76.

admit.ok_on_pace: a min_pace entry passes the pace gate when its pool's pace is known and >= min_pace and the pool's eligibleAccounts count, when present, is above 2
admit.behind_or_low: a min_pace entry fails the pace gate when its pool's pace is unknown or below min_pace, or when the pool's eligibleAccounts count is present and 2 or less; an entry with no min_pace has no pace gate
admit.critical: the same pace gate as behind_or_low (a count of 1 is 2 or less)
admit.exhausted: an entry whose pool is exhausted is skipped: its eligibleAccounts is 0, or, when the pool reports no count, its status is exhausted; a headroom label alone never skips it
admit.every_entry: paced or not, an entry is skipped when its model alias does not resolve, its seat is down, or it shares the author's vendor on a cross-vendor class; in a class that declares auditors it is also skipped when no auditor is declared for its vendor, the auditor's model does not resolve, the auditor's pool is exhausted (no eligible account) or has an eligibleAccounts count of 1 or less, or the auditor's seat is down; a pool counts as exhausted only when its eligibleAccounts is 0, or by its status label when it reports no count
